unit.why: The division is mostly a list of the Neskhizer tzaddik's customs about bad dreams, but it ends with a brief anecdote: he sees a townsman upset one morning, asks him why, and rules that he need not fast.
unit.boundary_note: Part of a run of divisions on dreams (מענין חלומות). The preceding division ends with the heading, and the next division continues the topic with a quotation from דודאים בשדה.

stories.start_quote: כשהיו מספרין לפני מרן הצה״ק מנעסכיז
stories.end_quote: יעו״ש מה שהארכנו בזה והוא נחוץ מאד
stories.summary_en: The Neskhizer tzaddik's customs for people with bad dreams (charity to R. Meir Baal HaNes, secret charity, a blessing instead of immersion on Yom Kippur night), and an anecdote in which he tells an upset townsman that he need not fast over a Shulchan Arukh dream unless his soul is grieved.

tags.why: Mainly a description and justification of customs, with only a minimal narrative.

quotes: מחמת שחלם לי מהחלומות המובאים בש״ע להתענות עליהם
tags.why: A character's dream triggers the anecdote.

quotes: ליתן ח"י ג״פ לצדקת ר״מ בעל הנס
tags.why: Charity is prescribed as the remedy for a bad dream.

quotes: אם אין נפשך עגומה עליך לא תתענה
tags.why: The question is whether to keep a dream fast (תענית חלום).
He gives a halakhic ruling about a fast prescribed in the Shulchan Arukh.
Immersion after a nocturnal emission is at issue, and he declines to require it.

quotes: ומי שארעהו החלום ר״ל בליל יוה״כ
tags.why: One of the customs is set on the night of Yom Kippur.
The man's distress after his dream is what the ruling addresses.

quotes: ולפרקים הי' מבין מי שרוצה לשאלו על זה
tags.why: He sometimes knew, without being told, who wanted to ask him.
